claims.statement: The revision noun rides two bindings: Card.version, encoded into the Telegram button by encode_callback_data as `p1:<card uuid hex>:<version>:<choice index>` (refused above 64 bytes) and decoded back by decode_callback_data, which Inbox._claim_locked compares against the live card after the expiry refresh and before the state check (refusing `stale_version`), and the card's recorded Telegram message identity (telegram_chat_id plus telegram_message_id, written by record_telegram_message only for the live version and `stale_message` on a mismatch), which is what an owner reply resolves against; update_request requires expected_version, refuses a mismatch and increments version.

Inbox._claim_locked is the single writer of an answer, entered only by the three owner-side doors (Inbox.claim for a tap, Inbox.claim_reply for an owner reply, Inbox.answer for the local owner credential) and never by a tool on the agent surface: a successful claim writes state="tapped", the choice and/or the reply text, responded_at and responded_via, and saves through _save before waking the parked calls (_notify_waiters) and before asking the destination to strip the keyboard (_request_strip, which swallows its own failures), so a failed strip cannot unrecord the answer.

responded_via records how an answer arrived and has three shipped values: `telegram` (the default of Inbox.claim, a tap), `telegram-reply` (Inbox.claim_reply) and `answer-path` (passed by the POST /answer route, the only production caller of Inbox.answer, whose own parameter default `owner` is never used); Inbox.record_tap defaults to `app` and has no production caller, so it is a test shortcut rather than a fourth answer path.

The owner noun resolves to two deliberately separate things: Inbox.owner_telegram_id, the only from.id that can become a tap and the only chat id a card is sent to, and the owner_answer_token credential checked by Inbox.check_answer_token on POST /answer (which refuses the create bearer explicitly); Inbox.answer then routes through claim with owner_verified=True so both surfaces share one implementation of the owner and version checks.

The inbox noun is the Inbox object plus the SQLite Store: one file `inbox.sqlite` in $XDG_DATA_HOME/paraphe else ~/.local/share/paraphe, directory mode 0700 and file mode 0600, with the location earlier releases used retained as the constant LEGACY_STORE_PATH (/var/lib/paraphe/inbox.sqlite); resolve_store_path refuses the default when a store exists only at that retained location rather than starting a second, empty inbox, while an explicit store_path is honoured either way.

The waited-call leg of the return path is wait_seconds (0-60, validated by _opt_wait) on the WAIT_TOOLS ask_question, request_approval and get_response: call_tool releases the inbox lock and parks in _park until the card leaves `open` or the window ends, returning the reading envelope; get_response and list_unprocessed read the same answers with no waiter and do not consume them.

The waiter-command leg of the return path is `paraphe wait <request_id>`: cli.wait_for_answer repeats the bounded get_response window until the card is answered or can no longer be answered, printing the answered envelope and exiting 0 answered, 3 expired or cancelled, 4 unknown request id.

ADR 0011 supersedes ADR 0003 and ADR 0006 and withdraws the gateway-wake machinery (no wake record, no wake attempt, no WakePort seam or adapter, source_thread descriptive only); the tree matches: src/paraphe/adapters/ holds console.py and telegram.py plus __init__.py, the adapter is a tap and answer destination, and no module, class or test implements a wake record, a WakePort or a gateway wake.

The AGENTS.md layout table's row for src/paraphe/adapters/ still lists "the wake port" as part of that directory, which the code and ADR 0011 no longer support, so the row is not an inventory of modules.

ADR 0009's cutover proof card still reads "tap -> the same Hermes session acts -> report_execution -> mark_processed" and cites ADR 0006 for that resumption, but the mechanism it leaned on is withdrawn: ADR 0011 leaves the parked call or a later run's read as the only ways the asking side acts, and docs/specs/paraphe-v1.md states that ADR 0011 wins where the two disagree.

source_thread is inert descriptive metadata: create and update only copy the validated caller string onto the card, nothing is woken from it, and nothing parses the Hermes origin records ADR 0006 specified (hermes:session:api_server:<id>, hermes:session:telegram:<id>) or the origin user stories that repeat them in the v1 spec.

The return-path protocol is carried to clients by the served text rather than by any per-runtime integration: TOOL_DESCRIPTIONS and _how_to_use in src/paraphe/inbox/__init__.py name request_id, wait_seconds, get_response, list_unprocessed, `paraphe wait`, the drain rule, the card-writing contract, the provenance fields and the reply rule; tests/inbox/test_surface_contract.py asserts those strings; and skills/paraphe-return-path/SKILL.md is the shipped per-runtime companion, giving the one copy step per runtime, the three ways to hold the return path with the waiter's exit codes 0/3/4, the waiter's environment, the provenance bounds and the shell-side create.

The tap-surface noun is implemented by the Telegram adapter accepting a callback only from a private chat whose id equals the owner id, so ADR 0002's rejection of a channel or chat topic as the inbox is enforced in code and every other chat is answered without a claim.

The owner-only Telegram /config command is recognised but not a settings editor: handle_update returns the canned reply "ttl and owner knobs only", Runtime.poll_once discards that return value, and no code writes settings, so changing knobs from Telegram remains planned by ADR 0008 while the credential-shaped part (strangers ignored, token never echoed) is implemented and tested.

Setup resolution is load_settings over a TOML file plus environment with the environment winning: the create bearer is required, an answer credential equal to the create bearer is refused, and a run needs either a bot token with the owner Telegram id (phone destination) or an owner_answer_token (local answer path).

Cutover is defined only by decision records and the spec (ADR 0004 and ADR 0009, sequenced in docs/specs/paraphe-v1.md: add the credential beside the previous inbox, prove tools/list, then switch endpoint and behaviour-block in one owner-approved window, with unattended batch callers staying behind); no module, entry point or test in the tree carries it.

Dropped product vocabulary survives as accepted-and-ignored input: rule_key is type-validated and dropped rather than refused, and the spec lists bulk approve, lock-screen chrome, Always-allow and responded_via: auto as dropped features.

The card noun is the Card dataclass (src/paraphe/inbox/card.py), whose persisted state is one of open, tapped, cancelled or expired, whose revision is version and whose life is expires_at / expires_in_seconds defaulting to 14400 with a 900-second floor and a 2_592_000-second ceiling enforced in src/paraphe/inbox/config.py.

The owner-reply channel is Inbox.claim_reply, which requires both from_id and chat_id to equal owner_telegram_id, resolves the card by the replied-to message id over the loaded card state (_card_by_telegram_message, so it still resolves after a restart and a reply to a superseded message resolves to nothing), and lets Inbox._claim_locked record the text verbatim with responded_via="telegram-reply" and the same lifecycle writes a same-moment tap makes.

The Telegram adapter's reply intake (TelegramAdapter.handle_update and _on_reply) turns a private-chat owner message whose reply_to_message names a message into a claim_reply call, swallows ClaimRefused and re-raises any other exception, so a refusal records nothing, raises nothing and wakes nothing while a real failure such as the durable write surfaces; a reply to a status message matches no card, and /config is handled only after the reply check.

Provenance is the PROVENANCE set runtime, repo, worktree and ticket: four optional bounded fields accepted by ask_question, request_approval, request_feedback and update_request, copied onto the card by _opt_shared / _apply_shared and taught in the served text and docs/tools.md, supplied by the caller and never guessed.

The identity line is _identity_line's rendering of the card payload: agent_name then runtime, repo, worktree and ticket in that order, absent fields omitted, with a ticket containing "://" rendered as a tappable link, so nothing is invented to fill a gap.

The rendered card is render_card in src/paraphe/adapters/telegram.py: fixed sections in a fixed order (identity line, kind line with a risk word, bold title, context, numbered options with notes, Recommended, If approved, Limits, links, reply hint, expiry), every interpolated value escaped and lone surrogates replaced, and the longest free-text sections trimmed with the visible TRIM_MARKER so the message fits MESSAGE_BUDGET (3800) under PLATFORM_LIMIT (4096) measured in UTF-16 code units, which keeps the renderer total instead of failing a send.

The words the card work added (owner reply, provenance and the identity line, the rendered card and its trim marker) come from the card work rather than from an ADR: docs/tools.md and the v1 spec revision carry them, the served how_to_use text teaches the reply channel as response.text with responded_via telegram-reply, and the requirements behind them — R1–R14 and the acceptance examples, which spell the section order, the escaping and the visible trim marker — live in docs/plans/2026-09-11-1604-feat-card-context-and-reply-plan.md; CONTEXT.md still carries only its original noun list, and no ADR replaces ADR 0007, which keeps a Telegram callback a claim rather than a decision.

The product noun Paraphe is the package src/paraphe/ exposed as the console script `paraphe = "paraphe.__main__:main"` in pyproject.toml: `paraphe` and `python3 -m paraphe` start the same service through paraphe.__main__, whose first argument dispatches ask/wait to paraphe.cli, check telegram to paraphe.check and store relocate to paraphe.store_cli, and every setting is spelled with the PARAPHE_ prefix.

AGENTS.md is the canonical instruction file for this repository, CLAUDE.md is a one-line pointer to it rather than a second copy, and the tracker and domain notes it points at live under docs/agents/ (issue-tracker.md, triage-labels.md, domain.md).

The create credential cannot answer a decision on any surface: no served tool name contains `answer` or `claim`, the POST /answer route checks the owner answer token with Inbox.check_answer_token (which refuses the create bearer by explicit comparison), and the served how_to_use text states that the credential creates and reads and cannot answer a decision.

relocate_store(source, target, move=False) is the safe move off the retained location: it copies through SQLite's backup API into a temporary file in the target directory, verifies PRAGMA integrity_check and the presence of the cards table, then installs the copy with the owner-only modes, refusing a missing or unreadable source, an occupied target and a source that is not a Paraphe store; `paraphe store relocate` wraps it to move LEGACY_STORE_PATH to the current default location, keeping the source as a backup unless --move is given.

`paraphe check telegram` (src/paraphe/check.py, reached through paraphe.__main__ before the server path, so it needs no running service) is the setup preflight for the phone half: it loads the same settings, resolves the bot identity through the Bot API, sends one plain setup message to the owner and names both, and exits 2 when no phone destination is configured, when the token is refused or Telegram is unreachable, or when delivery to the owner fails — never printing the token and never creating a decision card.
